items.reason: Added an operating committed-credential gate — `npm run security:secrets` reads every file git tracks against a 13-shape table (was 5, diff-only), wired as a blocking step in ci.yml's node-quality job on every push and PR, with `npm run test:security` fixtures that fire each pattern and scan the real tree; the same table now backs the constitution lens's `secret` rule, which a `Gate-exemption:` trailer can no longer waive. NOT closed, and it is a scanner false positive rather than work left undone: the 'dangerous workflow 0/10' sub-finding against agent-dispatch.yml and autofix.yml — neither has a single `${{ }}` inside any `run:` or `script:` body (every event value is passed through `env:`), neither uses pull_request_target or workflow_run, and `npm run security:actions` already blocks all three shapes on every push with fixtures in gate-check.test.mjs.

lessons: Adding a CI step to this repo is a four-file change, not one: .github/workflows/ci.yml, the `guidance.gates` list in .ai/manifest.yaml, a row in the AGENTS.md gate table, and the package.json script. `npm run guidance:check` compares all four in both directions and fails as `gate-unlisted` / `gate-stale` if any is missed.

This repository's escape hatches are commit trailers (`Gate-exemption:`, `Doc-sync:`, `Commit-convention-exemption:`) rather than per-line suppressions — good, but a trailer is written by whoever wrote the change, so a hatch that covers ALL blocking findings covers the ones an agent has a motive to waive. Ask of any new blanket waiver which specific findings it must not reach.

Before adding a pattern to a detector here, check it against the tree first: a rule whose first act is to fail the build on an existing fixture gets deleted rather than obeyed. Polar's `polar_whs_…` shape was left out of the credential table for exactly that reason and recorded as a named gap instead of quietly dropped.

Ascent's 'untrusted input in a run step' heuristic reports a step whose `env:` block carries `github.event.*` — which is the CORRECT fix for run-injection, not the bug. A repo that already has a stricter, fixture-backed check for the same class will keep scoring 0/10 on it; check the repo's own gate before treating that sub-score as work.
